scope: Independent design review only; no source inspection, code edits, remote calls, inference or training in this task.
architectural_concern: Determine whether removing time-objective gradients helps the fixed Cap MLP16 quantity task, while preserving the observed time inputs and shared representation. This is an objective ablation, not an input ablation or new backbone.
recommendation: Use the exact existing quantity_loss tensor as joint objective for alpha0. Preserve common initialization/RNG, model/input/head/optimizer settings, budget and Validation rawRMSE selection.

options.effect: No time-loss computational connection; time-exclusive parameters must have grad=None and remain unchanged under AdamW. Shared parameters still learn from quantity.
options.cost: Small new conditional objective path and explicit optimizer equivalence/state tests; existing stage and queue infrastructure reusable.

options.effect: Can produce materialized zero time-head gradients, allowing AdamW weight decay or residual optimizer state to change time-exclusive parameters; 0*nonfinite can also yield nonfinite joint.
options.cost: Slightly shorter implementation but changes the meaning and complicates interpretation.

required_checks_before_launch.check: Identity/equality test that alpha0 joint is quantity_loss itself; demonstrate time-exclusive grad is None after backward, and exact time-exclusive parameter/optimizer-state invariance after multiple optimizer steps. Use zero_grad(set_to_none=True); no warm start or resumed optimizer state.

Time-exclusive versus shared parameters must be defined from actual usage. Do not freeze common embeddings/encoder or remove observed time inputs. Shared representation and any shared state may change through quantity learning.
Retain the full existing model construction and RNG consumption so common initial tensors and data order match alpha1/.1/10. Do not remove time-head construction or reseed selectively.

Preserve the existing global clipping rule. Changed gradient norms and clipping frequency are consequences of objective removal and must be reported; this is not a claim that only direct gradient direction changes.

Keep unweighted recorded positive-integer TimeNLL as an explicitly untrained-time-head diagnostic. Initial time-head tensors may encode Train-derived initialization and are not necessarily random. Its output can change as shared h changes. Do not interpret its comparison as a trained time-prediction baseline or evidence that time information was removed.

Keep quantity loss/joint/quantity predictions finite requirements. Specify how an undefined or nonfinite diagnostic TimeNLL is reported: do not replace it with zero or silently discard the run. A nonfinite value in the unused time branch must not contaminate joint through multiplication by zero. Any diagnostic failure should remain explicit and separate from quantity training success.

Per host, require the predecessor18 assigned training and Validation stages complete, actual dispatcher exit0, and all predecessor-owned processes/GPU entries absent. Global GPU emptiness is not the requirement because the explicitly expected externalCap27 paused contexts remain. Validate those old identities remain T; reject unknown GPU owners.

New CPU waiter must not create CUDA context, run GPU qualification or start scientific workers before the host gate. Finite waiting must honor inherited absolute deadline; waiting does not restart the host budget. Gate failure/timeout must preserve evidence and stop without repeated launch, source overwrite or old signals.

After the gate, fresh ownership/free-memory qualification then exclusive launch intent; no race-prone duplicate workers. At most3 new scientific workers per host. Keep all old claims/source/checkpoints immutable.

Nine new fits exactly3datasets×seed42/52/62, planned4/5 split across5080/5090; same first strict finite fullValidation rawRMSE minimum, same-epoch MAE and TimeNLL, no Test and no baseline/CNN reexecution.

interpretation_boundaries: This contrasts joint-task training with quantity-only optimization while retaining time-history information. It does not isolate a backbone contribution.
A gain cannot by itself identify gradient conflict as the unique cause: task regularization, global clipping and AdamW updates also change.
Quantity RMSE/MAE can improve or trade off; evaluate both with all seeds and sample SD. Do not force success from one metric.
Alpha0 TimeNLL is descriptive for an untrained time head on a quantity-trained shared representation; a quantity gain does not establish a usable joint quantity/time model.
Existing alpha1/.1/10 are reused as fixed references; no re-selection using Test.
Respect current Cap27 inherited absolute deadlines; no automatic extension for wait or new9.
